**Three governance defects found by running the flow: stale-green gates, actor-check vs #124, index.jsonl merge gap**

**What**: Three governance defects surfaced on 2026-07-25 while shipping routine bookkeeping PRs (#322, #326). None came from reading the code — all three came from operating the flow. Tickets: **#328**, **#329**, **#330**.

**#328 — gate verdicts are never re-evaluated after the human approval they depend on.**
`issue-link` requires the referenced issue to carry `status:approved`, but it runs on PR-open, before any human could approve. Measured:
- PR #322: gate ran 15:44:15, issue approved 15:59:21 → fail, 15 min early
- PR #326: gate ran 15:58:47, issue approved 15:59:31 → fail, 44 s early

Both PRs were correct against correctly-approved issues. Manual `gh run rerun <id> --failed` fixes it; nothing in the UI says so, so a red PR looks rejected.
**The worse half is stale GREEN.** `--failed` only re-runs jobs that *failed*. A gate resolving to `warn` exits 0, reports green, and is therefore skipped by the rerun — its stale verdict never refreshes. `actor-check` evaluated PR #322 at 15:44 and returned `warn` (REQ-L5-2, "never fail on missing evidence") because no approval existed. The label landed at 15:59:21. The ~16:00 rerun skipped the job because it was green. **#322 merged carrying a verdict computed before the fact it exists to check** — re-evaluated post-approval it would have returned `fail`, exactly as #326 did. So the same race produces a visible false rejection and an invisible false acceptance, and only the visible one gets noticed. Invariant to establish: no gate verdict may be older than the approval it depends on, green ones included.

**#329 — `actor-check` L5 and #124 are mutually unsatisfiable at n=1 maintainer.**
Verbatim verdict on PR #326: `actor-check: fail — the approved label was self-applied by "csrinaldi" (matches the PR author) — self-approval is not allowed.` #124 requires approval to be a human signature applied by the maintainer; L5 requires approver ≠ author. With one maintainer, issue author = PR author = only approver, so the rule can never pass. It is not misfiring — it correctly reports a condition the operating model guarantees.
Currently harmless: `actor-check` is in `DETECTION_JOBS`, not in branch protection's required contexts (`issue-link`, `diff-size`, `local-checks`, `memory-gate`, `decision-gate`), so `mergeable=MERGEABLE`, `state=UNSTABLE`. **The risk is promotion**: epic M6 pairs #124 with governance hardening, and #324/M9 exists to justify promoting detection gates to required — promoting this one would make the repo unmergeable for its own maintainer, and hands every solo adopter a permanently-red check saying their approval is illegitimate. Options recorded in the issue: tier-aware degrade to warn at n=1; redefine as "distinct act" rather than "distinct actor"; accept + document in KNOWN-LIMITATIONS; require two maintainers. Recommendation: the first two. **Sequence with #328** — fixing #328 makes this fire on every PR.

**#330 — `.memory/index.jsonl` has no `.gitattributes` merge strategy.**
`.gitattributes` covers `/.memory/manifest.json merge=engram-manifest` (custom driver, registered by `brain:env:init`) and `/.memory/records/*.jsonl merge=union` (git built-in). `index.jsonl` has no rule, so it falls back to default text merge and conflicts whenever two branches both ran `memory:share` — which memory-gate makes near-certain. Observed merging main into `chore/issue-325-*`: manifest auto-merged, records auto-merged, `CONFLICT (content) in .memory/index.jsonl`.
Safe fix because `memory-format.md:26` says the index is "derived, regenerable, committed — a query accelerator, never authoritative", and `memory:reindex` exists. Verified live: after reindex, 1318 physical record lines → 1179 unique ids, index matched exactly, 0 duplicate ids. `memory-format.md:108` already documents union's dup-line failure mode and reindex as the remedy. Fix = one line, `/.memory/index.jsonl merge=union`; consider making `memory:share` run reindex as its last step so the index self-heals.

**Why**: Owner asked for the tickets after the re-trigger friction bit twice in one session and the merge conflict exposed the third.

**Where**: `.github/workflows/governance.yml:44-95` (issue-link); `brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.mjs` (L5 evaluator); `.gitattributes:5,10`; `brain/core/methodology/memory-format.md:26,108`; `brain/scripts/memory/cli.mjs reindex`.

**Learned**: (1) **Resolving a `.memory/` conflict**: never hand-merge `index.jsonl` — `git checkout --ours` then `npm run memory:reindex`, which rebuilds from records and dedups. Verify with `cat .memory/records/*.jsonl | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | sort -u | wc -l` equalling `wc -l < .memory/index.jsonl`. (2) `gh run rerun <id> --failed` is **not** a general "refresh the checks" command — it silently leaves green-but-stale verdicts in place. To force a full re-evaluation, rerun without `--failed` or push an empty commit. (3) All three defects were invisible to code reading and only appeared under operation — which is itself the argument for #324/M9 (`brain:metrics`): governance quality is not observable without running it and measuring.
